preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless alveolar stop [t] to the glottal fricative [h]: the oral closure is lost and only glottal friction remains. In Liverpool English (Scouse) pre-pausal /t/ is realized as [h] in a small set of high-frequency function words such as it, lot, that and what, a pattern that Clark and Watson (2016) find stable across generations.

examples.note: Pre-pausal /t/ is debuccalized to [h] in Liverpool English, mainly in a small set of high-frequency function words.
The constraints on pre-pausal [h] have stayed stable in Liverpool across generations.

sources: Clark, L., & Watson, K. (2016). Phonological leveling, diffusion, and divergence: /t/ lenition in Liverpool and its hinterland. Language Variation and Change, 28(1). https://doi.org/10.1017/S0954394515000204
